workspace.research_question: Will sodium-ion batteries reach cost parity with lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells for stationary grid storage by 2030?

claims: Na-ion cell cost per kWh falls to or below LFP by 2030
Na-ion cycle life is sufficient for daily grid cycling
Na-ion manufacturing reaches the scale needed for parity
counter_hypotheses: Low lithium carbonate prices keep LFP cheaper through 2030
Na-ion manufacturing scale stays too small to reach parity

claims.label: Na-ion cell price, 2025
claims.quote: Average sodium-ion cell prices reached 87 USD/kWh in 2025, against 74 USD/kWh for LFP.

claims.label: LFP cell price, 2025
claims.quote: LFP cells for stationary storage averaged 74 USD/kWh across 62 buyers in 2025.

claims.label: Parity already reached
claims.text: Sodium-ion cells are already cheaper than LFP for grid storage in 2025.
claims.quote: Average sodium-ion cell prices reached 87 USD/kWh in 2025, against 74 USD/kWh for LFP.

claims.label: Parity year (base case)
claims.text: Sodium-ion reaches cell cost parity with LFP between 2028 and 2031 in the base case.
claims.quote: In the base case, sodium-ion cells reach cost parity with LFP between 2028 and 2031.

claims.label: Material cost advantage
claims.text: Sodium-ion cathode and current-collector materials cost 20-30 % less than LFP at scale.
claims.quote: materials costs are 20-30% lower than for LFP once production exceeds 50 GWh per year

claims.label: Current price premium
claims.text: Sodium-ion cells carry a 10-20 % price premium over LFP in 2025.
claims.quote: Buyers reported a premium of 10 to 20 percent for sodium-ion cells over comparable LFP cells.

claims.label: Lithium price sensitivity
claims.text: If lithium carbonate stays below 15,000 USD/t, LFP remains cheaper than sodium-ion through 2030.
claims.quote: Below 15,000 USD per tonne of lithium carbonate, LFP keeps its cost lead through 2030.

claims.label: Cycle life at 80 % retention
claims.quote: Cells retained 80% of initial capacity after 6,000 full cycles at 25 °C.

claims.label: Fit for daily cycling
claims.text: Sodium-ion cycle life is sufficient for 15 years of daily grid cycling.
claims.quote: sufficient for more than 15 years of daily cycling in stationary service

claims.label: Announced capacity
claims.text: Announced sodium-ion manufacturing capacity exceeds 150 GWh per year by 2030.
claims.quote: Announced capacity totals 162 GWh per year by 2030, of which 31 GWh is under construction.

claims.label: Main bottleneck
claims.text: Hard-carbon anode supply is the main constraint on sodium-ion scale-up.
claims.quote: hard-carbon anode supply, not cathode precursors, is the binding constraint on scale-up

claims.label: Recommendation
claims.text: Plan 2030 procurement on LFP pricing, and keep sodium-ion as a qualified second source to re-evaluate each year against lithium carbonate prices.

pairwise_summaries.intervention: Na-ion reaches cell cost parity with LFP by 2030
pairwise_summaries.summary: Na-ion cells still cost 10-20 % more in 2025. Models place parity between 2028 and 2031, and low lithium prices push it later.

grade.risk_of_bias: Serious: two of four sources are industry reports.
grade.inconsistency: Serious: parity year ranges from 2028 to after 2030.
grade.imprecision: Serious: results depend on wide lithium price scenarios.
grade.publication_bias: Suspected: vendor sources favour early parity.

pairwise_summaries.intervention: Na-ion cycle life is sufficient for daily grid cycling
pairwise_summaries.comparison: Na-ion cycle life is too short for grid duty
pairwise_summaries.summary: One peer-reviewed test of 24 cells reports 6,000 cycles at 80 % retention.

grade.indirectness: Not serious: laboratory duty cycle matches grid use.

pairwise_summaries.comparison: Scale-up is constrained by hard-carbon supply
pairwise_summaries.summary: Announced capacity is large, but only a fifth is under construction and hard-carbon supply limits growth.

synthesis.analysis: Evidence does not support parity today: Na-ion cells cost about 87 USD/kWh against 74 USD/kWh for LFP. Parity by 2030 is plausible in the base case, but it depends on lithium carbonate prices and on hard-carbon supply. Cycle life is not the limiting factor.

recommendation.text: Plan 2030 procurement on LFP pricing, and keep sodium-ion as a qualified second source to re-evaluate each year against lithium carbonate prices.
